draft.title: Thermoregulation
card: Thermoregulation is the control of body temperature. The body keeps its core temperature close to 37°C, at rest and in exercise.
the widening of blood vessels near the skin. More blood flows close to the surface, so more heat is lost to the air. The skin often looks flushed.
the narrowing of blood vessels near the skin. Less blood flows close to the surface, so less heat is lost and the core stays warm.
Exercise makes the muscles produce extra heat. The body responds with vasodilation and sweating, which helps it lose heat. In the cold, vasoconstriction helps it keep heat.
draft.remember: Widen to lose heat. Narrow to keep heat.

a.q: Lena is cold and still after waiting outside on a winter morning. What happens to the blood vessels near her skin?
opts: They narrow, so less heat is lost from the skin
They widen, so less heat is lost from the skin
They narrow, so more heat is lost from the skin
They widen, so more heat is lost from the skin
a.why: In the cold, the vessels near the skin narrow. This is vasoconstriction. Less blood reaches the surface, so less heat is lost. Widening would send more warm blood to the skin and cool her further.
a.clue: In the cold, the body wants to keep its heat.

b.q: Sam finishes a hard 5 km run on a warm day. His face looks red. What best explains this?
opts: Vessels near his skin widened, letting more heat escape
Vessels near his skin narrowed, letting more heat escape
Vessels near his skin widened, helping his body keep heat
Vessels near his skin narrowed, helping his body keep heat
b.why: Running makes his muscles produce extra heat. Vessels near the skin widen, so more warm blood flows close to the surface and heat is lost. The red face is a sign of this. Narrowing would keep heat in, which is the opposite of what he needs.
b.clue: Hard exercise makes extra heat that the body must lose.

a.best: They narrow, so less heat is lost from the skin

b.best: Vessels near his skin widened, letting more heat escape
